Disease Outbreak Hits Vietnam Construction Materials Industry, Disrupting Operations

A sudden outbreak of dengue fever has affected workers at several construction materials manufacturing sites across southern Vietnam, causing significant operational disruptions. Among the companies impacted is Vicem Ha Tien Cement JSC, one of the largest cement producers in the region.

According to the Vietnam Construction Materials Association, at least 15% of the workforce at major plants in Dong Nai and Binh Duong provinces have reported symptoms or have been placed in quarantine since the start of June. “Production schedules have been revised downwards, with several plants operating at reduced capacity,” said Nguyen Van Quang, spokesperson for the association. He added that the outbreak is straining already tight labor resources as the industry enters its peak season.

Vicem Ha Tien Cement JSC confirmed that it has temporarily suspended operations at one of its grinding units to allow for deep cleaning and disinfection. “Our priority is the health and safety of our employees,” a company representative said. “We are working closely with local health authorities to contain the situation and minimize disruption.”

Several mid-sized firms, including Saigon StoneWorks Ltd., have also reported absenteeism rates exceeding 20%. The Construction Materials Workers Union is urging companies to provide additional protective measures and paid sick leave. “Our members are concerned about both their health and lost earnings,” said union leader Le Thi Hoa.

Industry analysts warn that if the outbreak continues, more sites could face temporary closures, further impacting output and project timelines. The situation remains fluid as companies and health officials monitor developments daily.
